newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Judges criticised for Brazil's wage hike ruling.
newsitem.headline: Judges criticised for Brazil's wage hike ruling.

text.p: Brazilian newspapers on Thursday lashed out at a high court ruling granting a public sector wage hike, saying it threatens Brazil's stabilization drive.

"The court's decision is a irremediable mistake. By not understanding what is going on in the economy, the judges disrespect the rights of the whole society," said columnist Miriam Leitao in today's edition of O Globo newspaper.
Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) Wednesday dealt a blow to the government's cost-cutting drive by voting 6-4 in favour of a wage claim by 11 civil servants.
The 11 civil servants claimed that they were entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise awarded to the armed forces in 1993.
The court ruling sets a precedent for the full federal workforce to benefit from the measure if they bring their own cases against the government.
Although the government noted it would take steps if the ruling was extended to the entire federal workforce, officials said the decision should be respected.

Local newspapers, however, said the STF's move raised strong criticism from President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, who expressed his dissatisfaction with the court ruling. "They do not think about Brazil," Cardoso was quoted as saying in a private meeting.
